dimensions.assessment: Affects holders of existing BLM rights-of-way, state governments, Indian Tribes, public entities, and the Bureau of Land Management.
dimensions.evidence: acting for the holder or on behalf of a State, political subdivision of a State, Indian Tribe, or public entity

dimensions.assessment: Relieves certain non-profit water transporters from seeking secondary approvals and paying additional rents, while imposing a 30-day notice requirement.
dimensions.evidence: exempts holders from paying additional rents to the BLM for any use of such authorizations

dimensions.assessment: Exempts qualifying entities from paying additional BLM rents, though no exact dollar impact on federal revenue is provided.
dimensions.evidence: exempts holders from paying additional rents to the BLM for any use of such authorizations

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Aquifer Recharge Flexibility Act to clarify and broaden the permitted uses of existing public land authorizations.
dimensions.evidence: Subsection (c)(3) of the Aquifer Recharge Flexibility Act (43 U.S.C. 390g-9) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent operational clarification for existing and future right-of-way uses regarding water transport on public lands.

missing_information: The exact monetary value of rents waived under the exemption.
The total number of existing right-of-way holders that will utilize this provision.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands existing right-of-way authorizations across Bureau of Land Management lands for aquifer recharge purposes on behalf of states, tribes, or public entities without requiring additional departmental approval or rent increases, provided notice is given.
